full_text:
A fox, pursued closely by hounds, slipped as he leaped over a high garden hedge. Desperate to break his fall and save himself from the stony ravine below, he reached out and clamped his paws tightly around a dense wild bramble bush.

The sharp thorns pierced his tender pads, tearing his flesh and leaving him covered in blood. Howling in agony, the fox cried out:

"Cruel bush! I reached for you as a friend to save me from falling, and you have wounded me worse than the hounds!"

The bramble shook its thorny boughs and replied: "You were a fool to grasp me, neighbor Fox! Did you not know that it is my very nature to cling to and scratch everything that comes near me? Never expect gentle protection from that which lives by wounding others!"
moral: It is foolish to seek refuge in what is naturally armed to hurt whatever touches it.
